# Market open briefing — Friday 23 October 2026

## Overnight

Yields fell 19bp overnight and equities softened modestly, with small caps and the Dow leading declines, suggesting a flight to safety amid the bond rally rather than fundamental equity weakness. VIX edged up 2.5% despite muted index moves, consistent with repositioning around what appears to be technical support rather than fresh macro deterioration.

_Not found in this morning's tape or headlines: `2.5%`. The lede is model-written; the tables above are not._

## The tape

The dominant story is a 17bp bull steepener in the belly-to-long end, with 10s at 4.96% and fed funds futures already pricing 16bp of hikes by December — the curve is simultaneously rallying and pricing in more Fed tightening, suggesting a flight-to-duration bid rather than a dovish pivot read. WTI breaking above $101 while gold holds $4,039 and the dollar barely moves (+0.09%) means the bond rally is not being driven by deflation fear; energy is keeping stagflation risk alive. Equity futures are soft but not broken — the Dow and Russell both -0.40% with VIX at 19.53 (+2.57%) signals mild risk-off rotation out of cyclicals and small caps, consistent with a market digesting higher-for-longer odds against a stubborn commodity complex.

## Talking point of the day

> The 3m10s spread has widened to +74bp — re-steepening from the front end after a prolonged inversion — while 17bp of the long-end rally happened in a single session with oil above $101. That combination tells you the bond market is not buying a clean soft landing: you can get duration relief and a commodity inflation problem at the same time, and that tension is exactly what's keeping the VIX bid even as the index itself barely moves.
